worksheet.title: Finish the Stack
worksheet.subtitle: Add the missing block to reach the star
worksheet.learning_goal: I can choose the missing block that gets Bit to the star.

parts.title: One block is missing
parts.text: Each program has one empty block. Pick the move block that gets Bit to the star ★. Run the whole stack from the top to check where Bit lands.

parts.title: Finish Program A
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1. After ➡ ➡ Bit is on box 3. Which block finishes the program so Bit lands on the star (box 4)? Circle ➡ or ⬅, then draw it in the empty block.

parts.title: Finish Program B
parts.prompt: The empty block is in the MIDDLE this time. Which block makes Bit land on the star (box 4)? Circle ➡ or ⬅, then draw it in the empty block.

parts.title: Stage 2 — Bit on box 4, star on box 2
You try — Program C
parts.prompt: Now Bit starts on box 4 and the star is on box 2, to the LEFT. After ⬅ Bit is on box 3. Which block finishes the program so Bit lands on the star? Circle ➡ or ⬅, then draw it in the empty block.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: To finish a program, pick the block that makes it do the job. Always run the whole stack to check Bit lands where you want.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Finish the Stack
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children complete a partial block program by choosing the one move block that makes Bit reach the star, then run the whole stack to confirm. This is early program design: picking the instruction that produces the intended result, and testing it.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children select and test instructions to reach a goal.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles ➡ or ⬅ and draws the arrow in the empty block.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet, a pencil, and a blue crayon. Optional: floor boxes 1-5 with a movable star so the child can test the chosen block.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: on Program A, run ➡ ➡ together to box 3. 'Bit is on box 3 but the star is box 4 — one more step right. The missing block is ➡.'
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — children circle ➡ and draw it. Exercise 2 — the gap is in the middle, but the answer is still ➡; run the whole stack to confirm box 4.
3. YOU TRY: Exercise 3 — the star is now to the LEFT (box 2), so the missing block is ⬅.
4. Connect: 'Programmers add the block that finishes the job — then they run it to make sure.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — Program A: missing block is ➡ (box 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, the star).
Ex 2 — Program B: missing block is ➡, in the middle (box 1 → 2 → 3 → 4).
Ex 3 — Program C: missing block is ⬅ (box 4 → 3 → 2, the star).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common trap: picking ⬅ in Ex 1-2 because it is offered — have the child run the stack and see Bit move away from the star.
Ex 3 reverses the direction; re-anchor 'the star is on the LEFT now, so Bit goes ⬅.'
Simplify: do Programs A and C only (clear right / clear left).
Extend: ask what the missing block would be if the star moved to box 5 in Stage 1 (still ➡, and Program A would need two more steps).
Movement option: walk the fixed blocks on the floor, then let the child choose the last step to land on the star.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child draws ➡ for Programs A and B and ⬅ for Program C, and can run each completed stack to show Bit landing on the star.
